newsitem.title: USA: Nebraska crops aided by rain, warm weather.
newsitem.headline: Nebraska crops aided by rain, warm weather.

text.p: Rain and warm weather aided Nebraska crops during the week ended Sunday, according to the Nebraska Agricultural Statistics Service.
Severe storms, hail and high winds damaged crops in a few areas in western, south central and southeastern areas.

Corn improved during the week with 16 percent rated excellent, 66 good, 16 fair and two poor. Corn growth moved at a rapid pace due to rain and above normal temperatures. Corn borer moths were reported across the state.
Winter wheat was about unchanged with four percent rated excellent, 43 good, 39 fair, 12 poor and two very poor.
About 75 percent of the wheat had turned color versus 69 a year ago and the 79 average. Harvest could begin in the south central section the first of July.
Soybeans were 95 percent emerged versus 95 a year ago and the 95 average. The crop was rated 11 percent excellent, 66 good, 21 fair and two poor.
Sorghum was rated 10 percent excellent, 56 good, 29 fair and five poor.
Oats were rated nine percent excellent, 57 good, 30 fair, and four poor. Eighty-eight percent of the acreage had headed.
Pastures and ranges were rated three percent excellent, 60 good, 24 fair, 12 poor and one very poor.
Topsoil moisture was eight percent surplus, 74 adequate, 17 short and one very short.
